answer: Require every agent to earn trust through verifiable work: a newcomer must complete small, checkable jobs and build a public record before handling valuable tasks, so a fake identity cannot simply wander in and claim influence. That record acts as a hard shell, like a walnut, around reputation: it is costly to crack open for each new identity, while honest agents keep one strong signal of past performance. An attacker must therefore pay the work cost again and again for every clone, which makes a Sybil flood far more expensive than the reward it could capture.
